q: The practice of growing different crops in systematic succession on the same piece of land over seasons is ____. (P6)
explain: Crop rotation breaks pest life cycles, balances nutrient uptake, and preserves soil fertility.
hint: Alternating different crops in a planned cycle.

q: Growing a legume crop (such as groundnuts or beans) in rotation improves soil fertility because legumes ____. (P6)
options: fix atmospheric nitrogen into soil via root nodules
explain: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules convert atmospheric N2 into plant-usable nitrates.

q: A farming system where a farmer grows crops and rears livestock concurrently on the same farm is ____ farming. (P6)
explain: Mixed farming uses animal manure to enrich crops and crop residue to feed livestock.
hint: Both crops and animals on one farm.

q: The removal of the top fertile layer of soil by flowing water or strong wind is known as soil ____. (P6)
explain: Soil erosion degrades farm productivity and creates destructive gullies across farmland.
hint: Washing or blowing away of topsoil.

q: A method of controlling soil erosion on steep hillsides by building stepped level terraces is called ____. (P6)
explain: Terracing reduces water runoff velocity and traps precious soil moisture on slopes.

q: Crop classification: Yam is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Yam is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Cassava is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Cassava is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Rice is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Rice is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Millet is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Millet is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Cowpea (Beans) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Cowpea (Beans) is botanically classified as a legume.

q: Crop classification: Groundnut (Peanut) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Groundnut (Peanut) is botanically classified as a legume and oil crop.

q: Crop classification: Oil Palm is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Oil Palm is botanically classified as a oil and cash crop.

q: Crop classification: Cotton is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
options: fibre crop used for making textile clothing
explain: Cotton is botanically classified as a fibre crop used for making textile clothing.

q: Crop classification: Coffee is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Coffee is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Tea is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Tea is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Sugarcane is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 6).
explain: Sugarcane is botanically classified as a sugar crop.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Sheep? [P6]
explain: Sheep provide wool and mutton for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Bees (Apiculture)? [P6]
explain: Bees (Apiculture) provide honey and beeswax for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Silkworm? [P6]
explain: Silkworm provide silk fibre for textiles for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Pigs (Swine)? [P6]
explain: Pigs (Swine) provide pork and bacon for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Goats? [P6]
explain: Goats provide chevon meat, milk, and leather for human consumption and industrial use.
